intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a morning exploring the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum over 1,500 years. Walk across Sultanahmet Square to the stunning Blue Mosque with its six minarets and exquisite Iznik tile interior. Hire a local guide for deeper historical context on Byzantine and Ottoman history.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Bazaar Food and Shopping Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Then head to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar to sample Turkish delight, saffron, dried fruits, and local spices. Engage with vendors, taste free samples, and learn about Ottoman trade history embedded in every corridor.

experiences.name: Bosphorus Sunset Cruise
experiences.description: Board a traditional wooden boat for a scenic cruise along the Bosphorus Strait, the waterway dividing Europe and Asia. Marvel at Ottoman-era palaces, ancient fortresses like Rumeli Hisarı, and elegant waterfront mansions called yalıs. Watching the sun set over two continents is a deeply memorable and historically rich experience.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Meyhane Dinner in Beyoğlu
experiences.description: Experience an authentic Turkish meyhane (tavern) dinner in the vibrant Beyoğlu neighborhood. Enjoy a spread of cold and hot meze dishes like hummus, stuffed grape leaves, and börek, followed by grilled fish or lamb. Pair the meal with rakı, Turkey's anise-flavored spirit, while soaking in live fasıl music — a true immersion into local food culture.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Istanbul Archaeology Museums
experiences.description: Spend a full day at Topkapi Palace, the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for 400 years, exploring its imperial treasury, harem quarters, and sacred relics. Combine the visit with the adjacent Istanbul Archaeology Museums, housing artifacts from ancient Troy, Egypt, and Mesopotamia. This is one of the richest historical complexes in the world.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and take the Havaist airport bus or metro to the city center (budget option ~50-80 TRY vs. ~600 TRY taxi). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour bakery or market near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Late-night simit (sesame bread ring) and ayran from a street vendor or 24-hour market near the hotel (~30-50 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival night simple. Exchange a small amount of currency at the airport for immediate needs. Download the Istanbul metro app and Google Translate with Turkish offline pack before landing.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from travel. After a leisurely breakfast, take a short walk along the beachfront near the hotel to get oriented. Visit a local neighborhood market or bazaar nearby to pick up snacks and water for the day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Bosphorus waterfront area. Take a local ferry (vapur) across the Bosphorus — one of Istanbul's most iconic and cheapest experiences (~15 TRY). Explore the Üsküdar district on the Asian side: stroll along the waterfront promenade, visit the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque (free), and enjoy views of the Maiden's Tower.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to the European side. Walk through a local neighborhood and explore a lively street market. Enjoy the sunset over the Bosphorus from a public waterfront bench.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a local bakery — simit, börek, and çay (tea) (~40-60 TRY)
meals.lunch: Balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from a boat vendor near the Bosphorus ferry docks (~50-70 TRY)
meals.dinner: Lokanta (traditional Turkish cafeteria-style restaurant) near the hotel — lentil soup, rice, and grilled chicken (~80-120 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Get an Istanbulkart (transit card) today — saves significant money on all public transport. Available at metro stations for ~50 TRY deposit plus credit.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Sultanahmet, Istanbul's historic heart. Start at the Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque (Ayasofya) — now a mosque, free entry for non-prayer times. Admire the stunning Byzantine and Ottoman architecture. Arrive early to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the Sultanahmet Square to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) — free entry. Then explore the Hippodrome of Constantinople and its ancient monuments (Obelisk of Theodosius, Serpent Column) — all free outdoor sights. Visit the Basilica Cistern nearby (entry ~200 TRY, budget-worthy for its dramatic atmosphere).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Arasta Bazaar adjacent to the Blue Mosque for souvenir browsing. Watch the sunset from the Sultanahmet Park with views of both iconic mosques.

meals.breakfast: Menemen (Turkish scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers) at a local café in Sultanahmet (~60-80 TRY)
meals.lunch: Döner dürüm (wrap) from a street-side döner stall near Sultanahmet (~60-80 TRY)
meals.dinner: Pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) at a budget pide restaurant in Sultanahmet or Sirkeci (~100-140 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for mosque visits — shoulders and knees covered. Women should carry a headscarf. Mosques are closed to tourists during prayer times (check daily schedule). Sultanahmet is reachable by tram (T1 line) from the city center.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapi Palace (entry ~500 TRY — book online to avoid queues). Explore the outer courtyards, the Imperial Council Hall, the Treasury, and the Harem (separate ticket ~300 TRY). This was the administrative heart of the Ottoman Empire for centuries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill to Gülhane Park — Istanbul's oldest public park, free entry. Enjoy a peaceful stroll among rose gardens and ancient plane trees. Then head to the Istanbul Archaeology Museums complex nearby (entry ~200 TRY) — three museums in one, housing ancient Greek, Roman, and Ottoman artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the waterfront to the Eminönü district. Watch the evening bustle at the Galata Bridge, where fishermen line the railings. Cross the bridge on foot for free views of the Golden Horn.

meals.breakfast: Açık büfe (open buffet) at a neighborhood tea house — cheese, olives, tomatoes, eggs, bread, çay (~50-70 TRY)
meals.lunch: Kumpir (stuffed baked potato) from a street stall in Eminönü or packed lunch from a bakery (~50-70 TRY)
meals.dinner: Kokoreç (grilled offal sandwich) or midye dolma (stuffed mussels) from street vendors near Eminönü (~40-60 TRY for a filling street food dinner)

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is closed on Tuesdays. Plan accordingly and swap days if needed. The Harem requires a separate ticket — highly recommended for history lovers.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Entry is free. Browse textiles, ceramics, spices, jewelry, and leather goods. Practice your bargaining skills — prices are always negotiable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to the Egyptian Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü — free to enter. Sample Turkish delight, dried fruits, nuts, and spices. Buy budget-friendly gifts here. Then walk to the New Mosque (Yeni Cami) adjacent to the bazaar — free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Take the tram to Karaköy and walk up to the Galata Tower area. Explore the charming streets of Galata neighborhood filled with independent shops, cafés, and street art. Climb the Galata Tower for panoramic views (entry ~300 TRY) or admire it from below for free.

meals.breakfast: Pastane (pastry shop) breakfast — tea, börek, and croissant (~40-60 TRY)
meals.lunch: Wet burger (islak burger) from Bambi or a street stall in Eminönü — Istanbul's unique steamed slider (~20-30 TRY each)
meals.dinner: Meyhane-style dinner at a budget tavern in Karaköy — meze plates, bread, and ayran (~120-160 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Beware of friendly strangers who offer to show you around — a common tourist scam. Keep your bag close in crowded bazaars.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or tram to Beyoğlu and walk up İstiklal Avenue — Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard stretching 1.4 km. Admire the 19th-century European-style architecture, browse bookshops, and watch the nostalgic red tram pass through the crowds. Visit the historic Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) arcade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the backstreets of Beyoğlu: Asmalımescit and Nevizade streets, known for their authentic meyhanes and local character. Visit the Pera Museum (entry ~200 TRY) housing Ottoman-era paintings and Anatolian weights — a compact but fascinating collection.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Taksim Square — the symbolic heart of modern Istanbul. Walk along the surrounding streets to experience local urban life. Catch a free outdoor performance or street musician if available.

meals.breakfast: Kahvaltı (full Turkish breakfast spread) at a local Beyoğlu café — eggs, cheese, olives, honey, clotted cream, tomatoes, cucumbers, tea (~80-120 TRY)
meals.lunch: Lahmacun (thin Turkish pizza) rolled with parsley and lemon from a neighborhood restaurant on İstiklal's side streets (~30-50 TRY per piece)
meals.dinner: Tantuni (spiced meat wrap) or mercimek çorbası (lentil soup) with bread at a budget eatery near Taksim (~70-100 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: İstiklal Avenue is extremely crowded on weekends. Visit the Pera Museum on a Wednesday when some Turkish museums offer discounted or free entry.

day_by_day.morning: Take a public ferry (vapur) from Eminönü or Beşiktaş to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — specifically Büyükada, the largest island (~60-80 TRY each way with Istanbulkart). The ferry ride itself is a scenic 1.5-hour journey through the Marmara Sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Büyükada on foot or by renting a bicycle (~100-150 TRY/hour) — no motorized vehicles allowed on the island. Visit the hilltop Aya Yorgi Church for panoramic views, stroll through Victorian-era mansions, and enjoy the peaceful pine-scented atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Istanbul in the early evening. Watch the city's skyline emerge from the sea as you approach — one of Istanbul's most magical views. Relax near the hotel upon return.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the ferry — simit and cheese from a bakery (~30-40 TRY)
meals.lunch: Fresh fish lunch at a waterfront restaurant on Büyükada — grilled fish, salad, and bread (~150-200 TRY, a splurge but worth it for the setting)
meals.dinner: Simple and filling dinner at a neighborhood lokanta near the hotel — köfte (meatballs), pilav (rice), and cacık (yogurt dip) (~80-110 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Ferries to the Princes' Islands run frequently but get crowded on weekends. Buy return tickets in advance at the ferry terminal. Bring sunscreen and water for the island visit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — arguably Istanbul's most magnificent mosque, built by the legendary architect Mimar Sinan in 1558. Free entry. Explore the surrounding complex including the tombs of Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent and his wife Hürrem Sultan.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill through the historic Zeyrek neighborhood — one of Istanbul's oldest and most authentic residential areas with Byzantine-era buildings and wooden Ottoman houses. Visit the Zeyrek Mosque (former Byzantine Church of the Pantocrator) — free entry.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Fener and Balat neighborhoods along the Golden Horn — colorful, photogenic, and full of history. Explore the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate (Ekümenik Patrikane) and wander the rainbow-painted streets of Balat.

meals.breakfast: Menemen with fresh bread at a traditional kahvaltı salonu (breakfast house) near Süleymaniye (~60-80 TRY)
meals.lunch: Kelle paça çorbası (tripe soup) or lentil soup at a traditional soup restaurant (çorbacı) in the historic peninsula (~40-60 TRY)
meals.dinner: Meze and grilled fish at a budget meyhane in Balat — a local neighborhood restaurant away from tourist areas (~100-150 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Balat is increasingly popular with photographers and tourists but remains authentic. Visit on a weekday for a more local experience. The neighborhood has many antique and vintage shops worth browsing.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul via ferry to Kadıköy — Istanbul's trendiest, most bohemian neighborhood. Explore the lively Kadıköy Market (Kadıköy Çarşısı) — a food lover's paradise with fresh produce, cheeses, meats, pickles, and local delicacies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll along Moda neighborhood's coastal promenade — a favorite of local Istanbulites. Visit the Moda Park for a relaxing break. Explore the independent bookshops, vintage stores, and street art of Kadıköy's backstreets.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Kadıköy's vibrant nightlife street — Barlar Sokağı (Bar Street) — which comes alive in the evening with live music spilling from bars. Enjoy a budget-friendly evening of people-watching and street food.

meals.breakfast: Kadıköy Market breakfast — fresh bread, local cheeses, olives, tomatoes purchased directly from market stalls (~50-70 TRY)
meals.lunch: Çiğ köfte (spiced bulgur wraps) and ayran from a street stall in Kadıköy (~30-40 TRY)
meals.dinner: Izgara köfte (grilled meatballs) with shepherd's salad and bread at a local köfteci restaurant in Kadıköy (~90-120 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: The ferry to Kadıköy from Eminönü or Karaköy runs every 15-20 minutes and costs very little with the Istanbulkart. Kadıköy is known for its progressive, artsy vibe — very different from the historic peninsula.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Modern Art Museum in Karaköy (entry ~200 TRY) — Turkey's premier contemporary art museum with rotating exhibitions of Turkish and international artists. Located in a striking building on the Bosphorus waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Karaköy waterfront to Beşiktaş. Visit the Çırağan Palace exterior and gardens (free to walk past — it's now a hotel but the grounds are stunning). Continue to Ortaköy — a charming waterfront neighborhood famous for its baroque mosque and lively square.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Ortaköy waterfront at sunset — one of Istanbul's most photographed spots with the Bosphorus Bridge dramatically lit in the background. Browse the weekend craft market stalls (if operating).

meals.breakfast: Açma (soft pretzel-like pastry) and çay from a street cart near Karaköy (~20-30 TRY)
meals.lunch: Kumpir (giant stuffed baked potato loaded with toppings) from Ortaköy's famous kumpir stalls — the neighborhood's signature dish (~80-100 TRY)
meals.dinner: Midye dolma (stuffed mussels) and street food snacks along the Ortaköy waterfront (~50-80 TRY for a filling street food spread)

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Modern may be closed on Mondays — check ahead. Ortaköy is best visited in the late afternoon and evening when the atmosphere is most vibrant. The Bosphorus Bridge lights up beautifully after dark.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Mosque) — a Byzantine masterpiece featuring some of the world's finest medieval mosaics and frescoes (entry ~200 TRY). Located in the Edirnekapı neighborhood near the ancient Theodosian Walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along a section of the ancient Theodosian Walls — 5th-century Byzantine fortifications stretching 6.5 km across the city. Free to explore. Head to the Eyüp Sultan Mosque and cemetery — one of Istanbul's most sacred Islamic sites. Take the historic Pierre Loti cable car up to the hilltop café for panoramic Golden Horn views (~30 TRY).
day_by_day.evening: Sip çay at the legendary Pierre Loti Café on the hilltop — a historic café visited by the French novelist Pierre Loti in the 19th century. Enjoy the sweeping views over the Golden Horn and the old city at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Neighborhood bakery near the hotel — pastry, boiled egg, and tea (~40-60 TRY)
meals.lunch: Gözleme (hand-rolled savory flatbread stuffed with cheese, spinach, or meat) from a local woman cooking at a street stall near Eyüp (~50-70 TRY)
meals.dinner: Kuzu tandır (slow-roasted lamb) or tavuk şiş (chicken skewers) at a local ocakbaşı (grill restaurant) in Eyüp or Fatih (~100-140 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for Eyüp Sultan Mosque — it is a highly revered site. The Chora Church may have restricted access if undergoing restoration work — check current status before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dolmabahçe Palace (exterior and gardens are free — interior entry ~600 TRY). If budget allows, take a guided tour of the opulent 19th-century palace that served as the administrative center of the late Ottoman Empire. The crystal staircase and 4.5-ton chandelier are extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Beşiktaş market area for local shopping and browsing. Walk along the Bosphorus coastal road toward Bebek — a wealthy waterfront neighborhood with beautiful views. Sit at a waterfront bench and watch the cargo ships and tankers pass through the strait.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Beyoğlu for a final evening exploration. Visit the historic Pera Palace Hotel lobby (free to enter and admire) — where Agatha Christie wrote Murder on the Orient Express. Walk İstiklal Avenue one last time and pick up any remaining souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Full Turkish breakfast (kahvaltı) at a Beşiktaş neighborhood café — the classic spread with multiple small dishes (~80-120 TRY)
meals.lunch: Balık sandviç (fish sandwich) from a vendor near Beşiktaş ferry terminal (~60-80 TRY)
meals.dinner: Celebratory budget dinner — Adana kebap with rice, salad, and ayran at a well-regarded kebap restaurant in Beyoğlu (~120-160 TRY)

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays. If visiting the interior, book tickets online to avoid long queues. Bebek neighborhood is a pleasant 30-minute waterfront walk from Beşiktaş.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul. Take a slow walk along the beachfront near the hotel for a last look at the Bosphorus or Marmara Sea. Visit a local neighborhood tea house (çayhane) for a final glass of Turkish çay and simit. Pick up any last-minute Turkish delight, baklava, or local spices as gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Head to the airport with ample time — allow at least 3 hours before international departure. Take the Havaist bus or metro from the city center to Istanbul Airport (budget option). Do final currency exchange or spend remaining Turkish Lira at airport shops.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul. Reflect on 13 incredible days of history, culture, and food in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Last Turkish breakfast — börek, cheese, olives, and çay at a neighborhood pastane (~50-70 TRY)
meals.lunch: Airport food or spend remaining TRY on Turkish snacks — baklava, Turkish delight, or a final döner wrap (~80-120 TRY)
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Airport (IST) is large — allow extra time for security and boarding. Duty-free at Istanbul Airport offers good prices on Turkish products like lokum (Turkish delight), tea, and ceramics. Keep some TRY for final transport and tips.

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront district. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night snack at the hotel or grab a quick bite from a 24-hour kebab stand near the airport during transfer — try a simple dürüm wrap for around 80-120 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer with your hotel in advance to avoid late-night taxi hassles. Keep arrival night simple — rest is the priority after a long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast. Once rested, take a gentle orientation walk along the beachfront promenade near Aegean Bliss Resort to get your bearings and breathe in the Bosphorus air. Visit a nearby local bakery for a traditional simit (sesame bread ring) and çay (Turkish tea) to ease into Istanbul life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearby Kadıköy district (if on the Asian side) or explore the Bosphorus waterfront. Visit a local bazaar or neighborhood market to sample fresh produce, spices, and street food. Browse colorful stalls and interact with vendors for an authentic first impression of Istanbul's daily rhythm.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed dinner at a waterfront meyhane (traditional Turkish tavern) near your hotel. Order a spread of cold mezze dishes such as haydari, patlıcan salatası, and arnavut ciğeri, paired with fresh bread.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet — enjoy olives, white cheese, tomatoes, cucumbers, eggs, and fresh bread included with your stay
meals.lunch: Street food exploration in the local market — try midye dolma (stuffed mussels), lahmacun (Turkish flatbread), and fresh juice for around 150-200 TRY
meals.dinner: Waterfront meyhane near the hotel — mezze spread with grilled fish for 400-600 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally light to help you recover from travel and jet lag. Keep the pace slow and exploratory. Exchange some currency at a local exchange office (döviz bürosu) for better rates than airport kiosks.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry across the Bosphorus to the historic Sultanahmet district — one of Istanbul's most iconic experiences. Begin at the magnificent Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya), a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum. Arrive early to beat the crowds and spend 1.5–2 hours exploring its breathtaking Byzantine mosaics and Ottoman architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk five minutes to the stunning Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii), admiring its six minarets and exquisite İznik tile interior. Then explore Sultanahmet Square and the ancient Hippodrome of Constantinople, viewing the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column. End the afternoon with a visit to the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı), the atmospheric underground Byzantine water reservoir.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Sultanahmet's atmospheric streets as the mosques light up at dusk. Enjoy dinner at a traditional Ottoman restaurant in the area before taking the ferry back to your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi — the legendary meatball restaurant near the Hippodrome, serving köfte with white beans and bread for around 200-250 TRY
meals.dinner: Matbah Restaurant or similar Ottoman cuisine restaurant in Sultanahmet — try Ottoman lamb stew and baklava for 500-700 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Hagia Sophia is free to enter as it is now an active mosque — dress modestly, cover shoulders and knees, and women should bring a headscarf. Blue Mosque is also free. Basilica Cistern charges around 200 TRY. Purchase an Istanbulkart transit card for ferry and public transport savings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapı Palace, the opulent heart of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Explore the Imperial Treasury (home to the famous Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond), the Harem quarters, and the sacred relics in the Pavilion of the Holy Mantle. Allow 3–4 hours for a thorough visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the Palace's rose gardens to the Istanbul Archaeological Museums, a world-class complex housing the Alexander Sarcophagus, ancient Anatolian artifacts, and tiles from across the Ottoman world. Then wander through Gülhane Park for a peaceful afternoon stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Grand Bazaar area for an early evening shopping experience before it closes (typically around 19:00). Browse carpets, ceramics, jewelry, and spices. Then enjoy dinner in the nearby Beyazıt or Laleli neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Konyalı Restaurant inside Topkapı Palace grounds — historic eatery with traditional Turkish dishes for 300-450 TRY
meals.dinner: Local lokanta (traditional Turkish canteen) near Beyazıt — order dishes by weight such as stuffed peppers, lentil soup, and pilaf for 200-300 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Topkapı Palace entrance is around 500-600 TRY; Harem requires a separate ticket of around 300 TRY. The Archaeological Museums are separate and cost around 200 TRY. Book Topkapı tickets online in advance to skip queues.

day_by_day.morning: Cross the Golden Horn to explore the vibrant Beyoğlu district. Start at Taksim Square and walk down the famous İstiklal Avenue, a 1.4 km pedestrian boulevard lined with 19th-century European-style buildings, churches, embassies, bookshops, and cafés. Ride the historic Tünel funicular — one of the world's oldest underground railways — at the bottom of the avenue.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming backstreets of Galata and Karaköy neighborhoods. Visit the medieval Galata Tower for panoramic 360-degree views of Istanbul spanning both the European and Asian sides, the Bosphorus, and the Golden Horn. Browse the eclectic art galleries, vintage shops, and independent cafés of Galata.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the lively Beyoğlu nightlife scene. Visit a rooftop bar for sunset cocktails with Bosphorus views, then dine at a contemporary Turkish restaurant in Karaköy.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a traditional Istanbul kahvaltı (breakfast) house in Karaköy — enjoy a full spread of cheeses, olives, eggs, honey, clotted cream, and pastries for 300-400 TRY
meals.lunch: Döner kebab or tantuni wrap from a popular street stall on İstiklal Avenue for 150-200 TRY
meals.dinner: Karaköy Lokantası or similar modern Anatolian restaurant — seasonal vegetables, slow-cooked meats, and local wine for 500-700 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Galata Tower entrance is around 300 TRY — go late afternoon for the best lighting. İstiklal Avenue is pedestrian-only except for the nostalgic red tram. The neighborhood is very walkable but wear comfortable shoes as streets are cobblestoned.

day_by_day.morning: Experience the legendary Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) at opening time when it is less crowded. One of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops, it is a labyrinth of carpets, lamps, ceramics, jewelry, leather goods, and spices. Practice your bargaining skills and soak in the atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 15 minutes to the Egyptian Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı), also known as the Spice Bazaar, located near the Golden Horn. Sample Turkish delight, dried fruits, nuts, teas, and spices. Purchase edible souvenirs here. Afterward, take a short ferry ride on the Golden Horn for scenic views of the old city skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque complex — the grandest mosque in Istanbul, designed by the legendary architect Mimar Sinan. Explore the mosque, its courtyard, and the surrounding külliye (complex) including the tombs of Suleiman the Magnificent and his wife Hürrem Sultan.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Havuzlu Lokanta inside the Grand Bazaar — a historic restaurant serving traditional Turkish home cooking for 250-350 TRY
meals.dinner: Tarihi Çiçek Pasajı (Flower Passage) or a meyhane in the Eminönü waterfront area — grilled fish sandwich (balık ekmek) and mezze for 300-450 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Egyptian Bazaar is open daily. Bargaining is expected in both bazaars — start at 50-60% of the asking price. The Süleymaniye Mosque is free to enter and open to visitors outside prayer times.

day_by_day.morning: Take a full-day Bosphorus cruise — one of Istanbul's signature experiences. Board a public ferry from Eminönü or Beşiktaş and cruise the strait separating Europe and Asia, passing Ottoman palaces, wooden yalı mansions, medieval fortresses, and charming fishing villages. The full round-trip public ferry to Anadolu Kavağı takes about 6 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark at Anadolu Kavağı, a quaint fishing village at the northern end of the Bosphorus. Hike up to the medieval Yoros Castle for sweeping views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea. Browse the village's seafood restaurants along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry back to the city as the sun sets over the European skyline — a truly magical view. Arrive back at Eminönü in the evening and head back to your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eat early as the ferry departs around 10:30
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at one of the seafood restaurants in Anadolu Kavağı village — catch of the day with salad and bread for 400-550 TRY
meals.dinner: Light dinner near the hotel — try a pide (Turkish flatbread pizza) at a local pide salonu for 200-300 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The public Şehir Hatları ferry to Anadolu Kavağı departs at 10:35 from Eminönü and costs around 100 TRY each way — pay with Istanbulkart. Private Bosphorus tours are also available for more flexibility at 800-1500 TRY. Bring a light jacket as it can be breezy on the water.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul to explore the charming Üsküdar district. Visit the iconic Kız Kulesi (Maiden's Tower), a small islet tower in the middle of the Bosphorus with a rich history of legends. Take a short boat to the tower and enjoy breakfast or tea at its café with stunning views of both continents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Üsküdar's traditional neighborhood streets, visit the Mihrimah Sultan Mosque by Mimar Sinan, and browse the local Üsküdar market. Then head to the trendy Moda neighborhood in Kadıköy — Istanbul's bohemian Asian-side district — for its independent cafés, bookshops, and street art.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the legendary Kadıköy food market (Kadıköy Çarşısı) for a food tour of the Asian side. Sample kokoreç (seasoned offal), wet burgers (ıslak hamburger), fresh lakerda (cured bonito), and artisanal cheeses from specialty shops.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Kız Kulesi café with Bosphorus views — tea, pastries, and light bites for 200-300 TRY
meals.lunch: Çiya Sofrası in Kadıköy — a legendary restaurant serving rare Anatolian regional dishes and unusual stews for 300-400 TRY
meals.dinner: Food tour through Kadıköy market — graze on various street foods and deli items for 200-350 TRY total

day_by_day.notes: Kız Kulesi (Maiden's Tower) charges around 150-200 TRY for the boat transfer and entry. Çiya Sofrası is an Istanbul institution beloved by food lovers worldwide — arrive early as it gets busy. Kadıköy is easily reached by ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace, the lavish 19th-century Ottoman palace on the European Bosphorus shore that served as the administrative center of the late Ottoman Empire. Marvel at its 285 rooms, 43 halls, and the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier gifted by Queen Victoria. Guided tours are mandatory and last about 90 minutes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Beşiktaş, a lively waterfront neighborhood. Explore the Çırağan Palace (now a luxury hotel) gardens for free, then visit the Yıldız Park — a vast forested hillside park with Ottoman pavilions, a lake, and beautiful May blooms. Visit the Yıldız Porcelain Factory Museum.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the upscale Nişantaşı neighborhood for an evening of window shopping along its elegant boutique-lined streets. Dine at a sophisticated Turkish restaurant in this fashionable district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Beşiktaş waterfront — try a classic balık ekmek (grilled fish sandwich) from the famous floating boats at the pier for 150-200 TRY, with a glass of şalgam (turnip juice)
meals.dinner: Nişantaşı restaurant — contemporary Turkish cuisine with Anatolian ingredients, 500-750 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires pre-booked timed entry tickets — approximately 600-700 TRY. Photography inside is restricted. The palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays. Yıldız Park is free to enter and perfect for a leisurely afternoon walk.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a traditional Turkish hammam (bathhouse) experience — a cultural ritual dating back centuries. Visit the historic Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built in 1584 by Mimar Sinan) or Cağaloğlu Hamamı for an authentic scrub, foam massage, and relaxation session. Allow 2–2.5 hours for the full experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Refreshed from the hammam, explore the Fatih district — Istanbul's most conservative and historically rich neighborhood. Visit the stunning Fatih Mosque complex, the Chora Church (Kariye Camii) with its extraordinary Byzantine mosaics, and the ancient Theodosian Land Walls that once protected Constantinople.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Balat and Fener neighborhoods along the Golden Horn — Istanbul's historic Jewish and Greek Orthodox quarters. Wander colorful streets of painted houses, visit the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople, and browse antique shops.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Local esnaf lokantası (tradesmen's canteen) in Fatih — home-cooked Turkish food served cafeteria-style, 150-250 TRY
meals.dinner: Balat neighborhood restaurant — try the area's famous muhallebi (milk pudding) for dessert; dinner at a local meyhane for 350-500 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Hammam experience costs 600-1200 TRY depending on the package chosen — mid-range option includes kese (scrub) and köpük masajı (foam massage). The Chora Church may have restricted access if restoration work is ongoing — check ahead. Balat is very photogenic and perfect for golden hour photography.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — a chain of nine car-free islands in the Sea of Marmara. Board a ferry from Kabataş or Bostancı to Büyükada (the largest island). Rent a bicycle or take a horse-drawn phaeton carriage to explore the island's Victorian-era wooden mansions, pine forests, and hilltop monastery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Büyükada — hike up to the Aya Yorgi Monastery on the island's highest hill for panoramic views of the Sea of Marmara and distant Istanbul skyline. Swim at one of the island's small beaches if the May weather permits, or simply relax in a waterfront café.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul in the early evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner near your hotel, reflecting on the peaceful contrast of the islands with the city's energy.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eat before catching the morning ferry
meals.lunch: Seafood restaurant on Büyükada waterfront — grilled sea bass, calamari, and salad for 400-600 TRY
meals.dinner: Neighborhood restaurant near your hotel — try İskender kebab (döner over bread with tomato sauce and butter) for 250-350 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Ferry to Büyükada takes about 90 minutes from Kabataş and costs around 100 TRY each way with Istanbulkart. Bicycle rental on the island costs 200-300 TRY for a few hours. No motorized vehicles are allowed on the island — it is a wonderfully peaceful escape. Check ferry schedules in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (İstanbul Modern) in Karaköy — Turkey's premier contemporary art museum housed in a stunning building on the Bosphorus waterfront. Explore its permanent collection of modern Turkish art and rotating international exhibitions. The museum café has exceptional Bosphorus views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Pera Museum in Beyoğlu, home to the famous Orientalist painting 'The Tortoise Trainer' by Osman Hamdi Bey and fascinating collections of Anatolian weights and measures and Kütahya tiles. Afterward, visit the historic Pera Palace Hotel — where Agatha Christie wrote 'Murder on the Orient Express' — for afternoon tea in its legendary Orient Bar.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Beyoğlu area — enjoy a leisurely dinner at a classic meyhane with live fasıl music (traditional Ottoman classical music). Order a full spread of hot and cold mezze, grilled meats, and end with Turkish coffee and dessert.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Istanbul Modern café — light lunch with Bosphorus views, 300-400 TRY
meals.dinner: Traditional meyhane in Beyoğlu with live fasıl music — full mezze dinner with rakı (anise spirit) for 600-900 TRY per person

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Modern entrance is around 200-300 TRY. Pera Museum entrance is around 150-200 TRY. Afternoon tea at Pera Palace is a splurge at 500-700 TRY but a memorable cultural experience. Reservations recommended for meyhane dinner with live music on a Saturday night.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul — revisit a favorite spot or explore somewhere you missed. Consider a peaceful sunrise walk along the Bosphorus waterfront near your hotel, watching fishing boats and tankers pass. Visit a local simit cart and tea house for a quintessential Istanbul morning ritual with locals.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping — visit a local ceramics shop for hand-painted İznik-style tiles, a spice shop for Turkish teas and dried herbs, or a confectionery for quality Turkish delight and baklava to bring home. Pack your bags and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.evening: Transfer to Istanbul Airport for your departure. Allow at least 3 hours before flight time for check-in and security. Enjoy one final Turkish tea or Turkish coffee at the airport before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final Turkish breakfast at a local kahvaltı house near the hotel — enjoy the full spread one last time for 300-400 TRY
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a neighborhood börek shop — try su böreği (layered pastry with cheese or meat) and ayran (yogurt drink) for 150-200 TRY
meals.dinner: Airport dining or an early dinner near the hotel before transfer — 300-500 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Istanbul Airport (IST) is located on the European side, approximately 35-45 minutes from most central districts by taxi or Havaist airport bus. Pre-book your airport transfer to avoid last-minute stress. Keep some Turkish lira for tips, last-minute purchases, and transport. Duty-free at Istanbul Airport is excellent for last-minute gifts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Istanbul Airport on Flight UA at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront district. Check-in, unwind with a welcome drink at the hotel bar, and settle into your suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at the resort — charcuterie board, Turkish mezze platter, and herbal tea to ease into the local flavors

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport meet-and-greet service and private chauffeur for a seamless arrival. Request early check-in preparation so your suite is fully ready upon arrival. Keep Day 1 light — rest is essential after a long flight.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely start with a lavish breakfast at the resort's terrace restaurant overlooking the Bosphorus. Afterward, take a private guided orientation walk along the beachfront promenade to acclimate to the city's atmosphere and sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury boat tour along the Bosphorus Strait — cruise past Dolmabahçe Palace, the Rumeli Fortress, and the iconic suspension bridges. Enjoy champagne and light canapés on board while your expert guide narrates Istanbul's layered history from the water.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's rooftop terrace. Dinner at Mikla, a celebrated fine-dining restaurant atop the Marmara Pera Hotel, offering modern Anatolian cuisine with panoramic city views.

meals.breakfast: Resort terrace breakfast — freshly baked simit, clotted cream (kaymak), honey, Turkish cheeses, olives, eggs cooked to order, fresh-squeezed pomegranate juice
meals.lunch: Gourmet mezze and grilled seafood served on the private boat
meals.dinner: Mikla Restaurant — tasting menu featuring Anatolian-inspired dishes such as lamb tartare, aged beef, and foraged herb salads paired with curated Turkish wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the Bosphorus private boat at least 48 hours in advance. Mikla requires advance reservations — request a window table for the best views. Dress smart-casual for dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Topkapi Palace — explore the Imperial Treasury, the Harem quarters, and the sacred relics pavilion with a specialist historian guide who provides exclusive access and deep context beyond the standard tour.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) with your private guide, marveling at its Byzantine mosaics, Ottoman additions, and the interplay of light through its massive dome. Follow with a stroll through the adjacent Sultanahmet Square and the Hippodrome of Constantinople.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Asitane Restaurant in the Kariye neighborhood — renowned for recreating authentic Ottoman imperial recipes sourced from 15th- and 16th-century palace kitchen records.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at Matbah Restaurant inside the Ottoman Hotel Imperial, steps from Topkapi — Ottoman-era dishes in a refined courtyard setting
meals.dinner: Asitane Restaurant — Ottoman tasting menu including dishes like stuffed melon with lamb and almond, saffron-scented rice, and historic desserts

day_by_day.notes: Hagia Sophia now functions as a mosque — dress modestly (shoulders and knees covered). Women should carry a headscarf. Arrive at Topkapi early to beat crowds. Private guide significantly enhances the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private tour of the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) with a cultural guide and personal shopper — navigate 4,000+ shops with expert curation, focusing on antique ceramics, hand-woven kilims, fine jewelry, and Ottoman calligraphy. Avoid tourist traps and discover master craftsmen's ateliers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) for a sensory immersion into Turkish spices, dried fruits, lokum (Turkish delight), and saffron. Then take a short ferry ride across the Golden Horn to explore the Eminönü waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Private Bosphorus dinner cruise on a luxury yacht — white-glove service, live classical Turkish music (ney flute and oud), and a multi-course dinner as you glide past illuminated palaces and mosques.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Traditional Turkish lunch at Pandeli Restaurant above the Spice Bazaar — one of Istanbul's oldest and most storied dining rooms, famous for its Iznik-tiled interior
meals.dinner: Multi-course dinner aboard the private yacht — cold mezze, grilled sea bass, lamb chops, and baklava for dessert with premium Turkish wines

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the personal shopper through the hotel concierge in advance. Pandeli requires reservations and is only open for lunch. The evening yacht dinner is a highlight — confirm weather and booking 3 days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Dolmabahçe Palace on the European shore of the Bosphorus — a breathtaking 19th-century Ottoman imperial palace with 285 rooms, 44 halls, and the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier. Private guided tour of the Selamlık and Harem sections.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the chic Nişantaşı neighborhood — Istanbul's answer to Paris's 8th arrondissement. Browse luxury Turkish and international boutiques, visit independent art galleries, and enjoy the tree-lined boulevards.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the historic Çırağan Palace Kempinski for sunset drinks on its legendary Bosphorus-side terrace. Dinner at Tuğra Restaurant within the palace — one of Istanbul's most opulent dining experiences.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Stylish lunch at Sunset Grill & Bar in Ulus — sweeping Bosphorus panoramas, exceptional grilled meats, and sushi bar
meals.dinner: Tuğra Restaurant at Çırağan Palace — Ottoman imperial cuisine in a gilded setting with live classical Turkish music; signature dishes include lamb tandir and palace-style stuffed eggplant

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays — verify the day of the week. Dress code at Tuğra is smart-elegant. Book well in advance as it is extremely popular.

day_by_day.morning: Full immersive hammam experience at the historic Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built 1584) or the Ayasofya Hürrem Sultan Hamamı — private cabin, traditional kese scrub, foam massage, and a relaxation session with herbal tea. A deeply cultural and rejuvenating experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided walking tour of the Beyoğlu district — explore the iconic Istiklal Avenue, the nostalgic red tram, art nouveau architecture, and hidden courtyards (pasajlar). Visit the Pera Museum to view its outstanding collection of Orientalist paintings and Kütahya tiles.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop cocktails at 360 Istanbul bar on Istiklal Avenue — panoramic 360-degree views of the city, Golden Horn, and Bosphorus. Dinner at Nicole Restaurant, a Michelin-recognized fine-dining destination in Tomtom Suites.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Artisan lunch at Karaköy Güllüoğlu — legendary baklava house with savory börek, cheese pastries, and the finest pistachio baklava in the city
meals.dinner: Nicole Restaurant — seasonal contemporary Turkish cuisine with French technique; expect dishes like black truffle-stuffed mushrooms, Aegean octopus, and lamb rack with wild herbs

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam's private VIP cabin in advance for the most exclusive experience. The Ayasofya Hürrem Sultan Hamamı is architecturally stunning and architecturally significant — highly recommended. Nicole's tasting menu should be reserved weeks ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — board a private speedboat from the resort's waterfront to Büyükada, the largest of the nine islands. Explore by horse-drawn carriage (phaeton), visit the historic Greek Orthodox Monastery of St. George atop the hill, and enjoy the car-free tranquility.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Büyükada's charming Victorian-era wooden mansions, stroll the pine-scented promenades, and relax on a quiet beach cove. Swim in the clear Marmara Sea waters.
day_by_day.evening: Return by private boat to Istanbul at sunset. Casual but refined dinner at a waterfront fish restaurant in the Arnavutköy neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most picturesque Bosphorus villages.

meals.breakfast: Packed gourmet breakfast basket prepared by the resort — enjoyed on the private boat en route to the islands
meals.lunch: Lunch at Splendid Otel's terrace restaurant on Büyükada — fresh grilled fish, calamari, and cold mezze with sea views
meals.dinner: Arnavutköy Balıkçısı or similar premium fish restaurant in Arnavutköy — whole sea bream or levrek (sea bass) grilled over charcoal, paired with rakı and cold meze

day_by_day.notes: The Princes' Islands trip takes approximately 45 minutes by private speedboat. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the monastery hike. Horse-drawn carriage rides should be booked on arrival at the island pier. Bring sun protection.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — the magnificent 6th-century underground Byzantine cistern with 336 marble columns. Recently renovated with dramatic lighting and art installations. Follow with a visit to the Istanbul Archaeology Museums — three world-class museums housing artifacts from Troy, Babylon, and ancient Anatolia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Balat and Fener neighborhoods on the Golden Horn — colorful Ottoman-era houses, Greek Orthodox Patriarchate, ancient synagogues, and a thriving arts scene. Private walking tour with a local cultural historian.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Ciya Sofrası in Kadıköy (Asian side) — legendary restaurant celebrated globally for its encyclopedic regional Anatolian cuisine, featuring rare dishes from southeastern Turkey rarely found elsewhere.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Charming lunch at a Balat café — homemade Turkish soup, gözleme (stuffed flatbread), and traditional ayran in the neighborhood's bohemian atmosphere
meals.dinner: Ciya Sofrası — order the daily specials board: lamb stew with quince, sour cherry kebab, and regional vegetable dishes; finish with homemade desserts like pumpkin in syrup

day_by_day.notes: Ciya Sofrası is on the Asian side — take a private water taxi across the Bosphorus from Eminönü for a scenic and quick crossing. The restaurant is casual but the food is extraordinary. Arrive early as dishes sell out.

day_by_day.morning: Private full-day excursion to Bursa — the first Ottoman capital, just 90 minutes by private ferry and car. Begin with the Grand Mosque (Ulu Cami) and the beautifully tiled Green Mosque (Yeşil Cami) and Green Tomb (Yeşil Türbe), masterpieces of early Ottoman architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Koza Han (Silk Cocoon Bazaar) — a stunning 15th-century caravanserai still trading in silk. Visit the Cumalıkızık village, a UNESCO-listed Ottoman village frozen in time. Take a cable car up Uludağ Mountain for panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by private ferry. Relaxed dinner at the resort's signature restaurant, reflecting on the day's journey.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Iskender kebab lunch in Bursa — this iconic dish of thinly sliced döner over bread with tomato sauce and browned butter was invented here; dine at Kebapçı İskender, the original family restaurant since 1867
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant — light Aegean-style dinner with fresh seafood and Turkish wines

day_by_day.notes: Bursa is a full-day commitment — depart by 8:30 AM. Arrange private car and driver in Bursa through the hotel. The Iskender kebab at the original restaurant is a once-in-a-lifetime culinary experience. Dress modestly for mosque visits.

day_by_day.morning: Private Turkish cooking class with a renowned local chef — held in a traditional Ottoman-style kitchen. Learn to prepare classic dishes: red lentil soup, stuffed grape leaves (dolma), lamb köfte, börek, and baklava. Includes a guided visit to a local market to select ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sakıp Sabancı Museum in Emirgan — housed in a magnificent Bosphorus-side mansion, featuring an outstanding collection of Ottoman calligraphy, paintings, and rotating international art exhibitions. Stroll through the adjacent Emirgan Park, famous for its tulip gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at the Rumeli Fortress (Rumelihisarı) — a spectacular 15th-century Ottoman fortress perched on the Bosphorus cliffs. Dinner at Feriye Palace Restaurant on the Bosphorus waterfront in Ortaköy.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of your morning cooking class — a full sit-down meal of everything you prepared, served with Turkish wines in the cooking school's dining room
meals.dinner: Feriye Palace Restaurant — Ottoman-European fusion cuisine in a 19th-century waterfront palace; signature dishes include sea bass in saffron broth and stuffed quail

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class should be booked at least one week in advance — request a private class for the most personalized experience. Feriye Palace has one of Istanbul's most romantic settings; request a Bosphorus-view table.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Süleymaniye Mosque complex — the grandest Ottoman mosque in Istanbul, designed by the legendary architect Mimar Sinan. Explore the mosque, the tombs of Sultan Süleyman and Roxelana, the historic medrese (theological school), and the panoramic terrace with sweeping Golden Horn views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive visit to the Topkapi Palace Harem (if not visited on Day 3) or explore the Istanbul Modern Museum in its stunning new waterfront building in Karaköy — Turkey's premier contemporary art museum with world-class rotating exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Private calligraphy or Ebru (Turkish paper marbling) workshop with a master artist in their atelier — a deeply meditative and culturally enriching experience. Dinner at Nusret (Salt Bae's flagship restaurant) for a theatrical premium steakhouse experience.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi — Istanbul's most iconic köfte restaurant, serving the same recipe since 1920 alongside white bean salad and ayran
meals.dinner: Nusret Istanbul — premium dry-aged tomahawk steak, gold-leaf butter, and signature salt presentation; pair with fine Turkish red wine

day_by_day.notes: The Ebru or calligraphy workshop is a wonderful souvenir activity — you leave with your own handcrafted artwork. Book through the hotel concierge. Nusret is a spectacle as much as a meal — reservations essential.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning at the resort — enjoy the spa facilities, indoor pool, or a private yoga session arranged on the beachfront terrace. Take a final Bosphorus swim if weather permits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping in Nişantaşı or the Grand Bazaar — premium Turkish ceramics from Paşabahçe, hand-embroidered linens, bespoke leather goods, fine silk scarves, and artisan jewelry. Visit a high-end Turkish delight shop like Hacı Bekir for premium confections to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the resort's finest restaurant — a curated tasting menu celebrating the best of Turkish cuisine, paired with a sommelier-selected flight of premium Anatolian wines. Arrange a private table on the Bosphorus-view terrace.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent resort breakfast — full spread with live cooking stations
meals.lunch: Elegant farewell lunch at Lacivert Restaurant in Anadoluhisarı on the Asian shore — stunning Bosphorus views, exceptional fresh seafood, and a peaceful garden setting
meals.dinner: Resort farewell tasting menu — seven courses featuring highlights of Turkish cuisine: Aegean octopus, Black Sea hamsi (anchovies), Anatolian lamb, and a dessert platter of Turkish sweets with aged rakı

day_by_day.notes: Request the farewell dinner setup in advance — the hotel can arrange flowers, personalized menus, and a photographer for a memorable final evening. Pack non-essential items tonight to ease tomorrow's departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — take a slow walk along the beachfront promenade, enjoy a last Turkish tea (çay) at the resort's seaside café, and soak in the Bosphorus views one last time. Light spa treatment or hammam session if time allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the resort with private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport. Depart with memories of one of the world's most magnificent cities.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — savor every bite of the Turkish breakfast spread: olives, cheeses, honey, kaymak, freshly baked bread, and strong Turkish tea
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or at the airport's premium lounge before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3.5 hours before departure for check-out, transfer, and airport procedures. Istanbul Airport is large — factor in extra time. The hotel concierge can assist with luggage storage if your flight is in the evening. Consider purchasing a bottle of premium Turkish wine or rakı at duty-free as a final souvenir.
